parsed.explanation: No traveler-facing universal exposure is documented: no presentation offence, no facility or border restriction, no custody rule, no criminalisation (2021 repeal stands unenforced even before it). The heaviest negatives are violence-adjacent and state-tolerated: trans people reported at over 4x assault risk, police dismissing complaints because the ID marker reads male, family pressure to drop cases, and slow committee referrals — practical impunity (tier 3: hostility with thin recourse). This is institutional failure, not state perpetration, and no organised targeting or universal state-imposed exclusion appears. Positive signals carry weight: decriminalisation, official SOGI-sensitive medical and GBV guidance (2020-21), documented absence of persecution beyond invisibility, and 2024 judicial/parliamentary engagement. Absent anti-discrimination law and suspended marker changes are mostly resident-side gaps; health-care refusal is the one setting that could touch a visitor. Net: elevated risk, above the 0.45 universal-exposure profiles, below 0.65 working-protection profiles.
